ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram there is an upper wire node/bus and a lower wire node/bus. The voltage U is marked on the left, and the arrow from top to bottom indicates that U is the voltage between the upper and lower two buses. In the middle branch, R1 and R2 are connected in series between the upper and lower buses; in the right branch, resistor R3 is also directly connected between the same upper and lower buses. Reasoning: Because the two terminals of R3 are respectively connected to the upper and lower buses, and the voltage U is exactly the voltage between these two buses, the voltage across R3 is U. The resistor power formula is P = V^2 / R. Substituting V_R3 = U and R = R3 gives P3 = U^2 / R3.
